Aristotle (Ancient Greek: Ἀριστοτέλης, romanized: Aristotélēs; 384–322 BC) was an ancient Greek philosopher and polymath.
In what year was Polyester discovered?
Polyester is a category of polymers that contain one or two ester linkages in every repeat unit of their main chain.
Information theory: Claude Shannon. Information theory is the mathematical study of the quantification, storage, and communication of a particular type of mathematically defined information.
Midazolam: Pfizer. It induces sleepiness, decreases anxiety, and causes anterograde amnesia.
In which country did the CAC/PAC JF-17 Thunder take place?
CAC/PAC JF-17 Thunder: People's Republic of China. The JF-17 can be used for multiple roles, including interception, ground attack, anti-ship, and aerial reconnaissance.
Who is credited with discovering Darmstadtium?
GSI Helmholtz Centre for Heavy Ion Research
Darmstadtium: GSI Helmholtz Centre for Heavy Ion Research. Darmstadtium is a synthetic chemical element; it has symbol Ds and atomic number 110.
Who is credited with discovering 2 Pallas?
2 Pallas: Heinrich Wilhelm Olbers. Pallas (minor-planet designation: 2 Pallas) is the third-largest asteroid in the Solar System by volume and mass.
Who is credited with discovering Multiple sclerosis?
Multiple sclerosis: Jean-Martin Charcot. It is a type of demyelinating disease, where the nervous system's ability to transmit signals is damaged.
Which European four-engine turboprop military transport plane, sized between the Lockheed C-130 and Boeing C-17, can land on rough airstrips and double as an aerial refueling tanker?
Airbus A400M Atlas is a European four-engine turboprop military transport aircraft. It can carry heavier loads than the C-130 and can use rough landing strips.
Before sharing the 2010 Nobel for graphene, this Manchester physicist won an Ig Nobel for levitating a frog using its own magnetism — who is he?
Andre Geim (born 21 October 1958) is a Russian-born British physicist working in England in the School of Physics and Astronomy at the University of Manchester.
Which noble gas, symbol Ar and atomic number 18, is the third most abundant gas in Earth's atmosphere — more plentiful there than carbon dioxide or neon?
Argon is a chemical element; it has symbol Ar and atomic number 18.
This facial hair grows on the jaw, chin, and cheeks, most commonly in adult men, though some women develop it too in a condition called hirsutism — name it?
Beard is the hair that grows on the jaw, chin, upper lip, lower lip, cheeks, and neck of humans and some non-human animals.
Dermatologists call the small version of this fluid-filled skin pocket a vesicle and the larger version a bulla; its English name traces back to an Old French word for a leprous nodule. What is it?

Blister is a small pocket of body fluid (lymph, serum, plasma, blood, or pus) within the upper layers of the skin, usually caused by forceful rubbing (friction), burning, freezing, chemical exposure or infection.
This English guard-dog breed combines the size of the Mastiff with genes from the extinct Old English Bulldog, and gained Kennel Club recognition in 1924 — which breed?
Bullmastiff is an English breed of dog of mastiff type and large size, with a solid build and a short muzzle.
Which Mediterranean evergreen tree, grown mainly in Spain, produces edible seed pods often ground into a chocolate substitute, with seeds that yield a gum used as a food thickener?
Carob (Ceratonia siliqua) is a flowering evergreen tree or shrub in the Caesalpinioideae subfamily of the legume family, Fabaceae.
This class of jawed fish — including sharks and rays — has a skeleton made almost entirely of cartilage, setting it apart from its bony-skeletoned relatives. What class is this?

Chondrichthyes (from Ancient Greek (khndros) 'cartilage' and (ikhths) 'fish') is a class of jawed fish that contains the cartilaginous fish or chondrichthyans, which all have skeletons primarily composed of cartilage.
This towering annual in the daisy family yields seeds in two flavors — oilseed (the world's fourth most-used vegetable oil) and the confectionary kind you crack as a snack — which plant?
Common sunflower (Helianthus annuus) is a large annual forb in the daisy family Asteraceae.
This term describes all the material inside a cell's outer membrane, excluding the nucleus (in cells that have one) — its main components include a gel-like fluid called the cytosol. What is it?
Cytoplasm is all the material within a eukaryotic or prokaryotic cell, enclosed by the cell membrane, including the organelles and excluding the nucleus in eukaryotic cells.
Tamed in Africa millennia ago and still hauling loads across the developing world, which equine traces its lineage to Equus africanus?
Donkey is a domesticated equine. It was domesticated in Africa some 5000–7000 years ago, and has been used mainly as a working animal since that time.
The tallest native bird in Australia and the third-tallest living bird overall, this flightless ratite can grow up to 1.9 metres tall. What bird is it?
Emu (Dromaius novaehollandiae) is a species of flightless bird endemic to Australia, where it is the tallest native bird.

Mostly caused by a mutation in the PRNP gene, this neurodegenerative prion disease begins with gradually worsening sleep trouble and progresses to total sleeplessness, speech and coordination problems, and death within months — which disease?
Fatal insomnia is a neurodegenerative prion disease that results in trouble sleeping as its hallmark symptom.
Named after a German militant group in a reader's 1994 letter and formalized by a Stanford linguist in 2005, this cognitive bias makes newly learned facts seem suddenly everywhere — what is it?

Frequency illusion (also known as the Baader-Meinhof phenomenon or Red Car Theory) is a cognitive bias in which a person notices a specific concept, word, or product more frequently after recently becoming aware of it.
Caused in over 90% of cases by iodine deficiency, this visible swelling in the neck comes from an enlarged thyroid gland — name the condition?
Goitre (British English, spelled goiter in American English) is a swelling in the neck resulting from an enlarged thyroid gland.
A Hollywood star of Algiers and Boom Town, this Austrian-American actress also co-invented a wartime radio guidance system — who was she?
Hedy Lamarr (born Hedwig Eva Maria Kiesler; November 9, 1914 - January 19, 2000) was an Austrian and American actress and inventor.

This condition occurs when cerebrospinal fluid builds up in and around the brain, in babies causing a rapid increase in head size and in the elderly causing poor balance and mental decline — what condition is it?
Hydrocephalus is a condition in which cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) builds up within and/or around the brain, which can cause pressure to increase in the skull.

This sudden bleeding into brain tissue or its ventricles is one of two major stroke categories, alongside the blockage-caused kind, and can trigger headache, one-sided weakness, or sudden speech and vision problems — what's the condition?
Intracerebral hemorrhage (ICH), also known as hemorrhagic stroke, is a sudden bleeding into the tissues of the brain (i.e., the parenchyma), into its ventricles, or both.
England's very first Astronomer Royal, he compiled a 3,000-star catalogue and even spotted Uranus — though he mistakenly logged it as a star. Who was he?
John Flamsteed (19 August 1646 - 31 December 1719) was an English astronomer and the first Astronomer Royal.
Native to southern China but long cultivated in Japan and Southeast Asia, this small fruit closely resembles an orange in color and texture but is only about the size of a large olive — what is it?
Kumquat are a group of small, angiosperm, fruit-bearing trees in the family Rutaceae.
Sociable for a big cat and more active by day than its relatives, this savannah hunter is so sexually dimorphic that only the males grow a sweeping mane. Which animal?
Lion (Panthera leo) is a large cat of the genus Panthera, currently ranging only in Sub-Saharan Africa and India.

This German sexologist founded the Scientific-Humanitarian Committee, which carried out what's been called the first advocacy for homosexual and transgender rights — before the Nazis stripped his citizenship in 1933. Who was he?
Magnus Hirschfeld (14 May 1868 - 14 May 1935) was a German physician, sexologist, and LGBTQ advocate whose German citizenship was revoked in 1933 by the Nazi government.
This natural biological transition marks the permanent end of menstrual periods, typically occurring between ages 45 and 55 as estrogen levels decline — what is it?
Menopause is the time when menstrual periods permanently stop, marking the end of the reproductive stage for the female human.
This Nissin Food Products founder invented instant chicken ramen and went on to create the Top Ramen and Cup Noodles brands — who is he?

Momofuku Ando (March 5, 1910 - January 5, 2007), born Go Pek-Hok (Peh-e-j: G Pek-hok; Ti-l: Go Pik-hok), was a Taiwanese-born, ethnic Chinese, Japanese inventor and businessman who founded Nissin Food Products Co., Ltd.

Distinguished from flatworms by having a digestive tract with openings at both ends, these free-living or parasitic roundworms make up their own entire phylum found in nearly every environment on Earth — what are they?
Nematode (or NEEM-; Ancient), roundworms or eelworms constitute the phylum Nematoda.
Founder of the charity Volnoe Delo and the industrial group Basic Element, which Russian oligarch led both En+ Group and Rusal until stepping down in 2018?
Oleg Deripaska (born 2 January 1968) is a Russian oligarch and billionaire.

Closely related to carrot and parsley, this pale, long-tapered root vegetable grows sweeter in flavor after winter frosts and produces yellow flowers if left unharvested into its second season — name the vegetable?
Parsnip (Pastinaca sativa) is a root vegetable closely related to carrot and parsley, all belonging to the flowering plant family Apiaceae.
Prized as an ornamental indoor plant and still poorly understood taxonomically, this arum-family genus ranks second in size only to Anthurium — which genus?
Philodendron is a large genus of flowering plants in the family Araceae.
This birth defect results in extra fingers or toes, occurs more often in the hands than the feet, and has been linked to more than three dozen genetic mutations — what is it?
Polydactyly (commonly known as sixth finger and extra finger) is a birth defect that results in extra fingers or toes.

Also called blepharoptosis and sometimes mistakenly called 'lazy eye,' this condition is marked by the drooping of the upper lid over the eye and can affect vision development in children if untreated — what is it?
Ptosis (eyelid) is a drooping or falling of the upper eyelid.
This long-term autoimmune disorder leaves joints warm, swollen and painful — typically the same ones on both sides of the body — and can stiffen worse after rest. What is it?
Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) is a long-term autoimmune disorder that primarily affects joints.

Native to the Azores, Europe, and the Middle East, this tree or shrub's flowers and berries have long been used for cordial and wine, and it also appears in traditional medicine and dietary supplements — name this plant?
Sambucus nigra is a temperate species of tree or shrub in the family Viburnaceae native to the Azores, Europe, and the Middle East.

Dubbed the "father of modern differential geometry," this Chinese-born American mathematician and poet won the Wolf Prize — and has a medal named for him by the International Mathematical Union. Who was he?
Shiing-Shen Chern (pinyin: Chn Xngshn; October 26, 1911 - December 3, 2004) was a Chinese-born American mathematician and poet.

Some versions allow a 'tie' or 'draw' while others insist on a single winner; it can pit hundreds against each other or just one person against the clock — what do we call this organized physical activity?
Sport is a physical activity or game, often competitive and organized, that maintains or improves physical ability and skills.
This West African berry contains a molecule that binds so powerfully to taste buds that sour foods eaten afterward taste sweet instead — what's this plant's common nickname?
Synsepalum dulcificum is a plant in the Sapotaceae family, native to tropical Africa.

One of five genera in the mackerel family whose members are collectively called tunas, this genus contains eight species, including the Atlantic bluefin, which can grow up to 15 feet long — name this genus?
Thunnus is a genus of ocean-dwelling, ray-finned bony fish from the mackerel family, Scombridae.
Caused by Salmonella Typhi bacteria and contracted orally, this disease presents with gradual fever, weakness, abdominal pain, and in severe cases, rose-colored skin spots. What is it?
Typhoid fever is an orally contracted disease caused by Salmonella enterica serotype Typhi bacteria, also called Salmonella Typhi.

In physics, this phenomenon occurs when two coherent waves combine according to their phase difference, producing either a boosted 'constructive' amplitude or a canceling 'destructive' one — what's the effect called?
Wave interference is a phenomenon in which two coherent waves are combined by adding their intensities or displacements with due consideration for their phase difference.
First synthesized by chemist Alexander Shulgin in 1974, this psychedelic compound produces hallucinogenic effects considered milder than LSD or psilocybin — what is it commonly known as?
2C-B: Psychedelic drug. 2C-B, also known as 4-bromo-2,5-dimethoxyphenethylamine or by names such as Nexus or Erox, is a psychedelic drug of the phenethylamine and 2C families.
Also known as the buckeye or conker tree, this deciduous flowering tree is often confused with the unrelated sweet chestnut — which species?
Aesculus hippocastanum: Species of tree in the soapberry family.
Defined by at least one carbon-carbon triple bond and traditionally nicknamed for its simplest member, ethyne (better known as acetylene) — which class of hydrocarbon is this?
Alkyne: Hydrocarbon compound containing one or more C≡C bonds.
This scientific discipline uses techniques from titration to mass spectrometry to identify unknown compounds and measure exactly how much of each substance is present in a mixture - which field?
Analytical chemistry: Study of the separation, identification, and quantification of matter.
This psychological state describes a lack of feeling, motivation, or concern, sitting on a spectrum between normal drive and akinetic mutism — what is it called?
Apathy: State of indifference, or the suppression of emotions.
First described in 1740 under the name Compositae, this enormous flowering-plant family includes daisies, asters and sunflowers — what is it?
Asteraceae: Large family of flowering plants.
One of the first grains ever domesticated, around 9000 BC in the Fertile Crescent, this cereal now ranks fourth in world production — and 70% of it goes to feeding animals — what is it?
Barley: Cereal grain. Barley (Hordeum vulgare), a member of the grass family, is a major cereal grain grown in temperate climates globally.
Split into structural biology, enzymology, and metabolism, this scientific field studies the chemical processes that occur within living organisms — which field?

Biochemistry: Study of chemical processes of living organisms. Biochemistry, or biological chemistry (distinct from chemical biology), is the study of chemical processes within and relating to living organisms.
Built as a militarized derivative of a popular 737 airliner, this maritime patrol aircraft hunts submarines for the US Navy and allies like India, Australia and the UK — which aircraft?
Boeing P-8 Poseidon: American maritime patrol aircraft. The Boeing P-8 Poseidon is an American maritime patrol and reconnaissance aircraft developed and produced by Boeing Defense, Space & Security.

Characterized by cycles of binge eating followed by compensatory behaviors like self-induced vomiting, this eating disorder has an estimated genetic risk factor between 30 and 80 percent — what is it called?
Bulimia nervosa: Eating disorder. Bulimia is more common among those who have a close relative with the condition.
Discovered in 1940 and making up as much as 40% of cannabis extract, this compound is an anticonvulsant used to treat two rare forms of childhood epilepsy — what is it?

Cannabidiol: Phytocannabinoid discovered in 1940. In the United States, the cannabidiol drug Epidiolex was approved by the Food and Drug Administration (FDA) in 2018, for the treatment of two seizure disorders.
Their young are calves and their castrated males are oxen; this widespread bovid is the most far-flung species of the genus Bos — what animal is it?
Its roasted root has long served as a coffee substitute, while today its extracted inulin shows up as a sweetener and fiber additive in packaged foods — which blue-flowered plant?
Chicory: Flowering plant in the daisy family.
Sold under the brand name Plavix, this antiplatelet drug taken after a heart attack or coronary stent placement kicks in within two hours and keeps working for five days — what is it?

Clopidogrel: Antiplatelet medication. Clopidogrel, sold under the brand name Plavix among others, is an antiplatelet medication used to reduce the risk of heart disease and stroke in those at high risk.
Renowned for a gift of mimicry noted by Pliny the Elder and Shakespeare, this glossy black bird has a bill that turns from black in winter to yellow in summer — what species is it?
Common starling: Species of passerine birds.
Surprisingly, the closest living relatives of birds are a clan of semiaquatic predators that includes alligators, caimans, and the long-snouted gharial. What is this reptile order?
Crocodilia: Order of reptiles. The teeth are conical and peg-like, and the bite is powerful.
This Manhattan Project physicist later led the Federation of American Scientists and is best remembered for his 1959 Senate testimony opposing Lewis Strauss's Commerce nomination — who is he?
David L. Hill: American nuclear physicist (1919–2008)
Named for the unique double-beamed bones under its tail, this long-necked Jurassic giant is one of the most common fossils found in North America's Morrison Formation. What dinosaur is it?
Diplodocus: Genus of diplodocid sauropod dinosaurs (fossil)
Named after the Greek word for 'hedgehog' because of its spiky central disk, this North American daisy relative is nicknamed the coneflower — what is it?
Echinacea: Genus of flowering plants in the daisy family.
Often triggered by contaminated food, NSAIDs, or autoimmune conditions like coeliac disease, which medical term describes inflammation of the small intestine?
Enteritis: Inflammation of the small intestine. Duodenitis, jejunitis, and ileitis are subtypes of enteritis which are localised to a specific part of the small intestine.

With a wingspan reaching 188 centimeters and distinctive ear tufts atop mottled blackish-and-tawny plumage, this raptor is one of the largest of its nocturnal kind, ranging widely across Europe and Asia — what bird is it?
Eurasian eagle-owl: Species of owl. The Eurasian eagle-owl (Bubo bubo) is a species of eagle-owl, a type of bird that resides much over Eurasia.
This Austrian-German automotive engineer built the first gasoline-electric hybrid car and designed the Volkswagen Beetle, but also contributed tanks to Nazi Germany's war effort — who was he?
Ferdinand Porsche: Austrian-born German automotive engineer, inventor (1875–1951)
Part of the rose family and prized for fruit that ranges from very sweet to notably tart, this genus's garden hybrid is an important commercial crop worldwide — which genus is it?
Found on every continent except Antarctica, these lizards are unusual for making vocal chirps and clicks, and most lack eyelids, relying on a transparent membrane instead — what are they?
Gecko: Lizards belonging to the suborder Gekkota.
One of the very first animals domesticated — in Iran some 10,000 years ago — this Bovidae cousin of the sheep now numbers over 1.1 billion worldwide, 150 million of them in India; what is it?
A founder of psychophysics, this German scientist captured how sensation relates to stimulus in a logarithmic law that now bears his and Weber's names — who was he?
Gustav Fechner: German experimental psychologist, physicist, and philosopher (1801–1887)

Spun into usable fiber some 50,000 years ago and, alongside bamboo, among the fastest-growing plants on Earth, which Cannabis sativa crop is grown for rope, paper, textiles and biofuel rather than for getting high?
These giant wasps of the genus Vespa build communal nests from chewed wood pulp, with one Asian species growing past two inches long — what are they called?
This mammal order today includes only small African and Middle Eastern hyraxes, but once boasted a species weighing up to 600 kilograms called Titanohyrax — which order?
Hyracoidea: Order of mammals. It includes the living hyraxes, placed within the family Procaviidae, and several extinct taxa.
Known naturally as the mineral hematite, this reddish compound with formula Fe2O3 is the main source for the steel industry and gets reduced by aluminum in the fiery thermite reaction — what is it?
Iron(III) oxide: Chemical compound. It occurs in nature as the mineral hematite, which serves as the primary source of iron for the steel industry.

This temporary condition throws your internal body clock out of sync with local time after rapid travel across multiple time zones — and most people find it harder to shake off flying east than west — what is it?

Jet lag: Condition due to travel across time zones. The phase shift when travelling from east to west is referred to as phase-delay of the circadian cycle, whereas going west to east is phase-advance of the cycle.
Developed for the Soviet Navy and known to NATO by a code name, this helicopter remains in service with several countries including Russia, Ukraine, and India -- which aircraft?
Commonly called the voice box, which organ in the upper neck houses the vocal cords and protects the windpipe from food entering it?
Larynx: Voice box, an organ in the neck of amphibians, reptiles, and mammals.
Creator of both a widely used open-source operating system kernel and the version-control system Git, this engineer won the 2012 Millennium Technology Prize — who is he?
Linus Torvalds: Finnish and American software engineer (born 1969)
Described in the New Testament as a physician, this traditional author of two New Testament books is said to have been martyred by hanging from an olive tree — who is he?
Luke the Evangelist: One of the four traditionally ascribed authors of the canonical gospels.

Often called the mirror image of depression, this psychiatric state brings racing thoughts, pressured speech, boundless energy, and a shrinking need for sleep — what is this elevated mood syndrome called?
Mania: State of abnormally elevated or irritable mood, arousal, and/or energy levels.
Developing from pigment-producing skin cells and most common on the legs in women and the back in men, about 30% of cases of this cancer arise from existing moles — what is it?
Melanoma: Skin cancer originating in melanocytes.
Succeeding the Castro brothers, this engineer became Cuba's first head of state in nearly six decades who wasn't a member of that family — who is he?
Miguel Díaz-Canel: Leader of Cuba since 2021.
Named for its rough alignment with the Moon's cycle — the two words are even linguistic cognates — this calendar unit varies from 28 to 31 days in the Gregorian system — what is it?
Month: Unit of time, usually 28 to 31 days.
Nicknamed the 'brain-eating amoeba,' this free-living microorganism lurks in warm freshwater lakes, hot springs, and poorly chlorinated pools — what is it?

Named for a mythological daughter of Tantalus, this silvery transition metal with atomic number 41 was once called columbium and is now prized as a nickel-free option in hypoallergenic jewelry — which element?
Niobium: Chemical element with atomic number 41 (Nb)
Born in Nishapur during the Seljuk era, this Persian polymath solved general cubic equations using intersecting conic sections centuries before Descartes — who was he?
Omar Khayyam: Persian polymath and poet (1048–1131)
A perennial herb from the mountains of East Asia, its root is the original source of a famous herbal supplement — though studies find little evidence it actually works. Which plant?
Panax ginseng: Species of flowering plant.
A famous singer known for her CCTV New Year's Gala appearances, she has served as China's First Lady since 2012 as the wife of its paramount leader — who is she?
Peng Liyuan: First Lady of China since 2012. Peng also sang the theme songs of several popular TV series, such as The Water Margin (1998).
Whether captured chemically on light-sensitive film or electronically by an image sensor, this art is fundamentally the practice of recording light — what is it?
Photography: Art and practice of creating images by recording light.
With a half-life of just 138 days, this rare radioactive element occurs only in trace amounts within uranium ore and is chemically similar to selenium — what is it?
Polonium: Chemical element with atomic number 84 (Po)
Encompassing peaches, cherries, plums, and almonds, this genus of flowering trees and shrubs in the rose family produces stone fruits called drupes — which genus?
Prunus: Genus of trees and shrubs.
Botanically a kin of spinach rather than a true grass, this protein-rich Andean pseudocereal was first cultivated near Lake Titicaca thousands of years ago — what is it?
Quinoa: Edible plant in the family Amaranthaceae.
Typically striking two to four weeks after a strep throat, this inflammatory disease can attack the heart, joints, skin and brain — and may permanently scar the heart valves. What is it?
Native to India, Nepal and Sri Lanka, this tiny feline is one of the smallest members of its family, and has been listed as Near Threatened since 2016 due to deforestation — which species?
Rusty-spotted cat: Small wild cat species native to South Asia.
Driven by an empirical cycle of observation, hypothesis, testing, and conclusion, this systematic discipline splits into natural and social branches. What is it?
Science: Systematic endeavour to gain knowledge.
Also called herpes zoster, this viral disease paints a painful blistering rash down just one side of the body, and can leave lingering nerve pain called postherpetic neuralgia — what is it?
Shingles: Viral disease caused by the varicella zoster virus.

Known as sun spiders, camel spiders, or wind scorpions, this arachnid order is neither true spider nor scorpion, and urban legends wildly exaggerate its size, speed, and danger to humans — what is it?
Solifugae: Order of arachnids. The order includes more than 1,000 described species in about 147 genera.
Known by the Reddit username 'spez,' this web developer co-founded the platform and also launched the now-defunct airfare search engine Hipmunk — who is he?
Steve Huffman: American web developer and entrepreneur (born 1983)
Also called the Java plum, this fast-growing evergreen tree from the Indian subcontinent can top 30 meters and live for over a century — which tree?
Syzygium cumini: Species of tree. It can reach heights of up to 30 m (100 ft) and can live more than 100 years.
Found in pufferfish, blue-ringed octopuses, and rough-skinned newts, this potent sodium-channel-blocking neurotoxin is also being trialed as a treatment for cancer-related pain — what is it?
Tetrodotoxin: Neurotoxin. Its name derives from Tetraodontiformes, an order that includes pufferfish, porcupinefish, ocean sunfish, and triggerfish; several of these species carry the toxin.
Nocturnal and tree-dwelling, this lizard species is native to Asia and various Pacific Islands — which reptile is it?
Tokay gecko: Species of reptile. The tokay gecko (Gekko gecko) is a nocturnal arboreal gecko in the genus Gekko, the true geckos.
Carrying the NATO nickname 'Backfire,' this supersonic Soviet bomber with variable-sweep wings first dropped conventional bombs during the Soviet–Afghan War — which aircraft is it?
Tupolev Tu-22M: Russian long-range supersonic strategic bomber.
Similar in size and mass to Earth, this planet has an atmosphere far thicker and denser than any other rocky body in the Solar System — and none of what?

Venus is the second planet from the Sun. Similar in size and mass to Earth, Venus has no liquid water, and its atmosphere is far thicker and denser than that of any other rocky body in the Solar System.
Packing a mass comparable to the Sun into a volume the size of Earth, this dense stellar remnant glows from leftover heat rather than nuclear fusion — what is it?
White dwarf: Stellar core remnant. A white dwarf is a very dense type of star: in an Earth-sized volume, it packs a mass that is comparable to the Sun.
Known by the formula ZnO, this white, water-insoluble powder shows up in sunscreens, calamine lotion, and rubber manufacturing — which compound?
Zinc oxide: White powder insoluble in water. Although it occurs naturally as the mineral zincite, most zinc oxide is produced synthetically.

The symbol for zinc is Zn. Zinc is a chemical element; it has symbol Zn and atomic number 30.

Kieran Culkin: Kieran Kyle Culkin (born September 30, 1982) is an American actor.

Dharmendra (8 December 1935 – 24 November 2025) was an Indian actor, producer and politician, primarily known for his work in Hindi films.

Aaron Taylor-Johnson: Aaron Perry Taylor-Johnson (né Johnson; born 13 June 1990) is an English actor.

MrBeast: James Stephen "Jimmy" Donaldson (born May 7, 1998), better known as MrBeast, is an American YouTuber, media personality, businessman, and philanthropist.

Bridget Fonda: Fonda is the daughter of Peter Fonda, niece of Jane Fonda, and granddaughter of Henry Fonda.
In what year did Kelly Preston die?
